BACKGROUND: The hosted @llm-canon test (frontend/e2e/scene-runtime.spec.js) loops `for (let index = 0; index < MAX_CANON_TURNS; ...)` with a hard-coded MAX_CANON_TURNS = 45, from when scenes advanced after ~3 turns. Pacing now holds each scene for several turns (data/stories/continuity-initiative/pacing.yaml: per scene min / nudge / handoff target turns, loaded by loadPackagePacing in package-clock.js via pacing.scenePoint(sceneId, 'handoff').target_turn and pacing.sceneOrder). In two hosted runs on 2026-10-15 the test used all 45 turns on scenes 1A-2C (6 scenes, 7-8 turns each) and then failed its own assertion 'the playthrough must visit every authored scene in order' with 3A, 3B, 3C unvisited. The turn cap, not the story, ended the run. Nine scenes at today's pacing need about 65-70 turns.

CHANGE:
1. In package-clock.js add and export a pure function canonTurnBudget(pacing, margin = ...) returning the largest number of turns the journey can legitimately need: the sum over pacing.sceneOrder of that scene's handoff target_turn, plus one extra turn per scene for the departure turn, plus a small fixed margin (default 5) for a valid non-progressing turn. Read how scenePoint/handoff work first; do not guess field names. It must throw a clear Error if a scene has no handoff point.
2. In scene-runtime.spec.js, the @llm-canon test must use canonTurnBudget(pacing) in place of the constant for its loop bound (pacing is already loaded inside that test). Leave SPINE_MAX_TURNS and the spine test alone. Remove or rewrite the stale comment on MAX_CANON_TURNS so it no longer claims 'up to three reveals each' as the justification; if the constant becomes unused, delete it. Keep MAX_STALLED_TURNS as is. Also confirm the test.setTimeout(20 * 60_000) is enough for the larger budget at the documented 90 s per-turn timeout ceiling in the worst case? It is not necessary to make it worst-case safe: only raise it if canonTurnBudget(real pacing) * 20 s would exceed it, and say what you did in your notes.
3. Tests in package-clock.test.js (node:test, existing style): canonTurnBudget on a small synthetic pacing object (sum of handoffs + one per scene + margin; margin override; a scene without a handoff throws), and one test that loads the REAL package pacing (loadPackagePacing for story 'continuity_initiative', as other tests in that file do) and asserts the budget is at least the sum of the real handoff targets and is greater than 45. Do not pin the exact number.
4. docs/testing-runbook.md section 7 says a run counts only with 'nine scenes and 30 or more turns'. Keep that floor but, if you can state it accurately, add that the loop bound is derived from the package pacing; make no other edits to the runbook (it must stay short, see its header).

HOW TO RUN: from the worktree `ln -s /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/frontend/node_modules frontend/node_modules` if missing (gitignored), then `cd frontend && node --test e2e/package-clock.test.js e2e/package-clock-controller.test.js e2e/canon-journey.test.js && node --check e2e/package-clock.js e2e/scene-runtime.spec.js`. Match surrounding style. Notes (the real budget number you computed, what you changed) to /home/bcorfman/dev/ringer-work/stage2-notes/canon-budget-notes.md.
